ar.title: لماذا نرى البرق أولًا؟ حيلة الـ 3 ثوان
ar.description:
لماذا نرى البرق قبل أن نسمع الرعد؟ البرق والرعد يحدثان في اللحظة نفسها، لكن الضوء أسرع من الصوت بكثير: الضوء يصلك في لحظة، والصوت يقطع حوالي كيلومتر كل 3 ثوان.
وهذه حيلة لحساب بعد العاصفة: عُدّ الثواني بين البرق والرعد واقسمها على 3، فتعرف المسافة بالكيلومتر.

#علوم #فيزياء #shorts
ar.first_comment: جرّب في العاصفة القادمة: كم ثانية عددت بين البرق والرعد؟ 👇

en.title: How Far Is the Storm? Divide by 3
en.description:
Why do you see lightning before you hear thunder? Both happen at the same instant, but light is far faster than sound: light reaches you almost instantly, while sound covers about 1 km every 3 seconds.
The trick: count the seconds between the flash and the thunder and divide by 3 to get the storm's distance in kilometers (divide by 5 for miles).

#science #physics #shorts
tags: why do we see lightning before thunder
en.first_comment: Next storm, try it: how many seconds did you count? 👇

hooks.ar: ترى البرق دائمًا أولًا، ثم يأتي صوت الرعد! لماذا؟
hooks.en: You see lightning before you hear it, every time. Why?
3 seconds of silence after lightning means 1 km. Why?
Lightning strikes once, but you get the news twice. Why?
You can measure a storm with just your fingers. How?
Count the seconds after lightning and you know how far it is. How?

test: new hook formula: a practical 'try it yourself' trick (count ÷ 3)
facts: Divide the seconds between lightning and thunder by 3 for kilometers (by 5 for miles) (NOAA JetStream 'Lightning safety / Fast Facts'; NWS 'Thunder').
Sound travels about 343 m/s in air (≈1 km per 3 s); speed varies with temperature (NOAA; NASA Glenn 'Speed of sound').
Light travels ~300,000 km/s, so the flash arrives practically instantly at storm distances (standard physics).
Lightning and thunder are produced by the same event (NWS 'Thunder').
No safety advice given in the video beyond the distance trick.
